svg.text: Digital Wallet & Ledger Evolution: 2021 Default vs. 2026 Modern Standard
From Custom mmap/RocksDB/HDFS Event Pipes & Hand-Rolled Phase Tables to TigerBeetle io_uring VSR, Temporal Sagas & WORM Ledgers
Architectural Dimension
2021 Textbook Baseline (ByteByteGo Ch. 27)
2026 Production Standard (Purpose-Built Financial Engines)
1. Core Ledger Engine
& Single-Node TPS
Custom Java/C++ mmap log + RocksDB LSM (~10,000 TPS/node)
Bespoke in-house Raft state machine + RocksDB wrapper requiring
200 partition groups to sustain 2,000,000 account-leg TPS
TigerBeetle (VSR + io_uring, 500k–1M+ TPS/node) or Spanner/CRDB
Fixed-size 128-byte Account/Transfer structs batched via io_uring
and Viewstamped Replication (or CockroachDB/Spanner Multi-Raft)
2. Two-Phase Pending
Holds (TC/C Primitives)
App-level TC/C Phase Status Tables & custom out_of_order flags
Every microservice team hand-rolls Try/Confirm/Cancel SQL tables,
hanging-try sweepers, and out-of-order Cancel tombstone logic
Native Ledger Two-Phase Transfers (PENDING / POST / VOID) + Temporal
First-class `flags.pending` with engine-enforced timeout auto-expiry
(`debits_pending` vs `debits_posted`) orchestrated by Temporal Sagas
3. Snapshot & Audit
Archive Storage
Self-managed Hadoop HDFS cluster for binary snapshots
High operational overhead of NameNodes/DataNodes; lacks native
hardware-enforced SEC 17a-4 WORM immutability attestation
Cloud Object Storage (S3 Object Lock WORM) + Merkle Hash Chain
Compliance-mode WORM snapshots + SHA-256 hash-chained event blocks
queried offline via Apache Iceberg / DuckDB for T+0 regulatory proofs
4. Correctness Proof
& Fault Verification
Post-hoc event replay + staging integration tests
Replaying events proves deterministic code changes, but rare storage
corruption or split-brain bugs surface only during real outages
Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST / VOPR) + Storage Fault Tolerance
Simulated network partitions, clock jumps, and directed disk sector
misdirected reads/writes tested across billions of seeds before deploy
5. CQRS Read Path
& Client Receipts
Custom Reverse Proxy + read state machine callback plumbing
Bespoke routing table mapping in-flight client sockets to partition
read projections to avoid client HTTP polling storms
LSN-Pinned Read-Your-Writes Gateways + Streaming Change Feeds
Synchronous commit returns the Raft log index (LSN token) directly
to the gateway while CDC change feeds update CQRS views in < 10 ms
Key Architectural Takeaway: Why Only the Immutable Event List Needs Consensus Replication
• Commands are non-deterministic external intents (may fail or depend on arrival order), whereas State (RocksDB) and Snapshots (S3/HDFS) are
100% deterministic projections of the validated Event log. Replicating ONLY the immutable Event log via Raft (or VSR) guarantees RPO = 0,
full historical point-in-time balance reconstruction, and zero-drift code-upgrade verification.
